contract_layers.native_exact_contracts: Direct instruction, local call-site, field-access, and object-layout facts that do not require root publication or runtime equality.
contract_layers.conditional_native_interpretations: Typed conclusions that hold when a receiver has the demonstrated layout, while root publication/liveness may remain unresolved.
contract_layers.modern_recommendations: Replacement architecture guidance such as a stable gameplay EntityId; these are not claims about an original native field or ABI.

scope.runtime_reason: The smallest static receiver/refcount separator resolves the local +0x54 contracts: the exceptional 0x00bff2d0 receiver is a separately published cSimulatorSpaceGame-shaped parent/context and its +0x54 field is mpHighLODPlanetSim, while 0x00b3d300 is a noun-manager-compatible raw root port whose result is consumed through cGameNounManager-layout fields. Follow-up-03 did not find a direct or bounded computed writer for DAT_0167eae0 or DAT_0167eb60 and did not close their publication, liveness, teardown, or value equality. Runtime would be required for those root-level questions and for save restoration timing, but is not required to describe the local accessor and replacement mechanics.

hypotheses.name: authoritative_gameplay_state
hypotheses.claim: When the receiver is the demonstrated cGameNounManager-layout object, its +0x54 value is the current intrusive gameplay-creature selection, not a disposable cache value. This does not establish which DAT_0167eae0/DAT_0167eb60 publication is live at runtime.
hypotheses.prediction: The owner must retain and release the selected creature, clear or replace it during lifecycle transitions, and consumers must reach authoritative creature fields such as target, health, brain level, locomotion, species profile, and progression-affecting state.
key_evidence: 0x00b1fd50 performs virtual +0x00 on the new value, stores it at owner+0x54, then performs virtual +0x04 on the old value.

0x00d2e4a0 dispatches a creature virtual method and reads creature+0xb5c; 0x00d2e580 reads locomotion and species state; 0x00d2e8a0 places the returned address in an action record consumed by 0x00d39360.
0x00c099e0 creates a cCreatureAnimal-compatible object and installs it through 0x00b1fd50 when the caller requests player/avatar state.

hypotheses.name: transient_runtime_pointer
hypotheses.claim: The accessor result is a transient borrowed view, but the noun-manager-shaped +0x54 storage is not merely an unretained cache: the demonstrated writer reference-manages the selected object.
hypotheses.prediction: A transient-only pointer would have no retained ownership, would be replaceable without affecting the authoritative noun, and would normally point to a presentation, index, or lightweight context rather than the full mutable creature object.
key_evidence: 0x00b1fdb0 is only a two-instruction read and therefore returns a borrowed/transient view of the stored word.
The same field is an intrusive owner reference: 0x00b1fd50 AddRefs the new object, stores it, and Releases the old object.
0x00c099e0 also inserts the creature into noun/parent collections, so the raw current pointer is one retention path rather than the object's whole ownership graph.

hypotheses.name: presentation_proxy
hypotheses.claim: The +0x54 value is a presentation/GFX proxy for the avatar rather than the gameplay creature itself.
hypotheses.prediction: Consumers should primarily resolve model, animation, world, or render handles; gameplay brain, health, locomotion, and target state should remain elsewhere; visual teardown should be able to replace the proxy independently.
key_evidence: Noun-manager consumers use the returned value as a cCreatureBase/cCreatureAnimal and reach gameplay state, not only render handles.
cCreatureBase+0xb54 is the separate intrusive_ptr<Anim::AnimatedCreature> presentation/animation association; cCreatureBase+0x150 is the model ResourceKey and +0x15c/+0x160 are model/world handles.
Cell has a separate GFX association and rebuild lifecycle at cCellObjectData+0x248, independent of cGameNounManager+0x54.

hypotheses.name: handle
hypotheses.claim: The returned word is an opaque ID, generation handle, pool index, or tagged union rather than an object pointer.
hypotheses.prediction: A handle should not support direct vtable loads and nested pointer dereferences, and replacement should not use virtual AddRef/Release on the value itself.
key_evidence: 0x00d2e380 loads result->vtable and calls slot +0xd8; 0x00d2e580 dereferences result+0xc0 and result+0xb20; 0x00d2e4a0 calls result vtable +0x84.
0x00b1fd50 invokes vtable +0x00 and +0x04 directly on the new and old words, requiring object addresses with refcount virtuals.
0x00d39360 uses raw pointer equality and ObjectTYPE kCreatureAnimal checks, not numeric range, map, or generation operations.

hypotheses.name: hybrid_typed_current_selection
hypotheses.claim: The local contract is hybrid: on a cGameNounManager-layout receiver, +0x54 is an intrusive current gameplay reference and 0x00b1fdb0 returns it without retaining; the creature carries runtime state plus a separate presentation association; Cell uses a pool index; and the tiny accessor body is reused across unrelated +0x54 fields. DAT_0167eae0/DAT_0167eb60 publication and equality remain unresolved.
hypotheses.prediction: Type-specific receiver provenance must determine the meaning of +0x54. Noun-manager-layout receivers yield cCreatureAnimal; the 0x01002bd0 receiver yields the cSimulatorSpaceGame +0x54 planet-simulation field. A stable gameplay EntityId is a modern replacement recommendation, not the observed native owner+0x54 contract.
key_evidence: 0x00b3d300 is a raw borrowed load of DAT_0167eae0, and the selected creature functions use that returned word immediately before 0x00b1fdb0.

0x00b20c60 and 0x00b21340 corroborate cGameNounManager fields +0x78/+0x7c, +0x98/+0x9c, and +0x10c/+0x110 in the same live-analysis session; they do not publish or equate DAT_0167eae0 with DAT_0167eb60.
Follow-up-03 found no direct or bounded computed writer, no cross-accessor equality, and four distinct four-byte root words; DAT_0167eae0 publication/liveness/teardown therefore remain open.

0x01002bd0 returns DAT_016dc0fc; 0x010066e0 publishes it with the cGonzagoSimulator/cSimulatorSpaceGame vtable pattern and 0x01006880 clears it. This is a separate publication chain, not evidence for either noun root.

0x00ef10c0 saves the current noun-layout avatar, clears owner+0x54, and destroys the old object; 0x00c099e0 creates/installs a new animal when the 0x00b3d300 port supplies a live noun-layout receiver.
The noun current pointer, cCellGame+0x411c avatar pool index, presentation handles, and save candidates are structurally distinct.

hypotheses.name: universal_avatar_accessor
hypotheses.claim: Every receiver of 0x00b1fdb0 is a cGameNounManager and every result is the current avatar.
hypotheses.prediction: All receiver+0x54 fields would have cCreatureAnimal/cCreatureBase semantics and all call sites would use creature gameplay or avatar state.
key_evidence: At 0x00bff3ad, 0x01002bd0 returns DAT_016dc0fc before 0x00b1fdb0 at 0x00bff3b4.
DAT_016dc0fc is the published cSimulatorSpaceGame object, and its +0x54 field is mpHighLODPlanetSim, not mpAvatar.
The result at that site is compared with the inherited EBX sentinel and otherwise only enables a separate 0x00ff5b30 call; it is not dereferenced as a creature.

adversarial_steps.name: receiver-type-separation
adversarial_steps.prediction: If 0x00b1fdb0 is universally GetAvatar, every receiver must be noun-manager-shaped. A receiver with a different exact vtable/size and a different +0x54 field type falsifies that claim.
evidence_for: Ten selected creature consumers obtain ECX from the 0x00b3d300 raw noun-root port and then call 0x00b1fdb0.
0x00b1fd50 receives a 0x00b3d300 result in its sampled callers and reference-manages +0x54.
0x00b21340 accepts that receiver family at cGameNounManager-layout noun fields, but this is a local type-contract result, not proof of DAT_0167eae0 publication or DAT_0167eb60 equality.
evidence_against: 0x00bff2d0 obtains ECX from 0x01002bd0 instead; that function returns DAT_016dc0fc.
0x010066e0 publishes DAT_016dc0fc using the 0xf0-byte cSimulatorSpaceGame cGonzagoSimulator vtable prefix, and 0x01006880 clears it on destruction.
cSimulatorSpaceGame+0x54 is mpHighLODPlanetSim, an intrusive_ptr<cSimPlanetHighLOD>, while cGameNounManager+0x54 is intrusive_ptr<cCreatureAnimal>.
adversarial_steps.independence: The exception separator combines a direct call-site dataflow, a separately published global, constructor/destructor writes, vtable bytes, and structure-layout metadata. These were correlated observations from the same analysis session and shared type vocabulary, not independent subagents or independent source lineages.
adversarial_steps.repetition: The ten b3d300-selected sites are repeated call-site evidence for one receiver family, not ten independent owner identities. The single exception is a distinct correlated observation that disproves universality; it does not resolve DAT_0167eae0 versus DAT_0167eb60 publication.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: 0x00b1fdb0 must remain a raw +0x54 accessor. Its semantic return type is receiver-dependent. The cCreatureAnimal contract is valid only for a receiver demonstrated to be cGameNounManager-layout; neither 0x00b3d300 publication nor 0x00b3d400/DAT_0167eb60 equality is established.

adversarial_steps.name: pointer-versus-handle
adversarial_steps.prediction: A stable ID or pool handle cannot be loaded as a vtable or passed to virtual AddRef/Release without prior resolution.
evidence_for: 0x00b1fdb0 returns a raw 32-bit owner field and does no lookup, generation check, or index resolution.
0x00d39360 carries the returned address in an action record and compares it by address.
evidence_against: 0x00d2e380 dereferences the returned value as a vtable and calls +0xd8.
0x00d2e580 dereferences +0xc0 and +0xb20; 0x00d2e4a0 dispatches +0x84.
0x00b1fd50 calls virtual +0x00/+0x04 on new/old words before/after the store.
adversarial_steps.independence: The direct dereferences, virtual dispatch, and replacement sequence come from different bodies, but all were correlated in the same live-analysis session. They are mechanically distinct observations, not independent evidence sources.
adversarial_steps.repetition: Several creature consumers repeat the same pointer-layout evidence; repetition strengthens the pointer result but does not independently prove the owner.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: Integer ID, generation handle, tagged union, and pool index are rejected for the noun-manager return. The ABI remains pointer-like and borrowed.

adversarial_steps.name: owner-versus-borrower
adversarial_steps.prediction: If +0x54 is owned, a writer must retain the new value before publication and release the old value after replacement; the getter must not retain on every read.
evidence_for: 0x00b1fd50 clears old+0xb58 bit 0x200, sets new+0xb58 bit 0x200, then AddRefs/stores/Releases when the address changes.
0x00c099e0 creates a cCreatureAnimal-compatible object and installs it for the player/avatar path.
0x00ef10c0 clears +0x54 before destroying the saved old object.
evidence_against: 0x00b1fdb0 itself performs no AddRef, so a caller retaining the raw result beyond the next replacement would be unsafe.
Other noun/parent collections may retain the same creature, so +0x54 is not necessarily its only owner.
adversarial_steps.independence: The exact local ownership mechanics come from the explicit virtual call order in 0x00b1fd50. Creation and reset bodies corroborate that sequence in the same session, not as independent evidence lineages; none closes root publication.
adversarial_steps.repetition: Two direct writer callers both source the receiver through 0x00b3d300; this repeats one root port and is not independent proof of aliasing or live publication relative to 0x00b3d400.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: For a live cGameNounManager-layout receiver, +0x54 is an intrusive current-selection slot and 0x00b1fdb0 returns its borrowed raw pointer. Same-pointer replacement performs no AddRef/store/Release; null replacement stores null and releases the old. The slot's publication through DAT_0167eae0 versus DAT_0167eb60 remains unresolved.

adversarial_steps.name: gameplay-versus-presentation-authority
adversarial_steps.prediction: If the noun pointer is a presentation proxy, direct consumers should resolve only model/animation/GFX state. Gameplay consumers should instead reach brain, locomotion, species, target, and action state, while presentation remains at cCreatureBase+0xb54 or separate GFX handles.
evidence_for: 0x00d2e4a0 calls creature vtable +0x84 with creature+0xb5c state.
0x00d2e580 reads species profile+0x61c and the locomotion subobject at creature+0xc0.
0x00d39360 checks ObjectTYPE kCreatureAnimal and pointer equality.
evidence_against: The returned creature itself contains model, AnimatedCreature, model-world, audio, and effect fields, so object and presentation graph are not wholly disjoint.
The exact detach/rebuild order for cCreatureBase+0xb54 was not traced in this investigation.
adversarial_steps.independence: Gameplay field access, vtable semantics, and creature structure fields are mechanically distinct but were collected in one same-session synthesis. Track-08's Cell GFX lifecycle is a separate artifact about a different domain, not independent proof of the noun pointer's meaning.
adversarial_steps.repetition: The same creature object naturally appears in both gameplay and presentation paths; that is the hybrid reason, not evidence that the current pointer is presentation-only.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: The noun pointer selects authoritative runtime gameplay state that also links to presentation. Presentation is a dependent association, not the meaning of owner+0x54.

adversarial_steps.name: current-pointer-versus-stable-identity
adversarial_steps.prediction: A stable entity identity would use a noun/definition ID, pool index, or generation. A current selection instead can be null or change while action records carry only the old raw address.
evidence_for: 0x00b1fd50 can replace or clear the word with no generation field at +0x54.
0x00d2e8a0 stores the current address in an action record; 0x00d39360 later compares that address to a fresh current value.
0x00ef10c0 saves, clears, and destroys the previous current object during a reset path.
evidence_against: cCreatureBase has definition/political IDs and a serializable interface, but the current-selection word is not proven to encode any of them.
A current pointer can remain stable between transitions, but stability is temporal rather than a persistent handle contract.
adversarial_steps.independence: The replacement body, action-record producer/consumer pair, and reset body are different control-flow paths, but all are correlated same-session static observations rather than independent sources.
adversarial_steps.repetition: Pointer equality in several action branches is repeated branch behavior, not evidence of a persistent identifier.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: owner+0x54 is current raw-object selection. No generation, pool index, or durable avatar ID is established at this field.

adversarial_steps.name: replacement-and-despawn-separation
adversarial_steps.prediction: Replacing the current selection, destroying the noun object, and rebuilding a Cell pool avatar are separate lifecycle operations.
evidence_for: 0x00b1fd50 implements atomic current-slot replacement with refcount operations and no destruction.
0x00c099e0 creates/configures a creature and then installs it as current.
0x00ef10c0 clears the current slot before the old object destruction path.
Cell despawn 0x00e780a0 clears cCellGame+0x411c only when the index matches, releases GFX/query state, optionally creates a replacement, and releases the pool entry.
evidence_against: The exact mode-level order between noun avatar teardown, persistence handoff, and presentation shutdown is not runtime-observed.
Cell and noun lifecycles can be coordinated by one mode, which can make the operations look merged from a caller.
adversarial_steps.independence: The noun writer, noun creator, noun reset, and Cell pool lifecycle are separate function bodies and state owners. The noun observations are same-session correlated evidence; the Cell evidence comes from a separate historical synthesis and concerns a different owner.
adversarial_steps.repetition: Many Cell despawn callers repeat the same pool cleanup, but that repetition does not establish noun-object destruction.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: Current-slot replacement, noun-object destruction, Cell despawn, and Cell reload/rebuild are distinct transitions.

adversarial_steps.name: pool-and-index-separation
adversarial_steps.prediction: The noun current avatar must not be represented by the Cell avatar index. The Cell current player is a local pool index; the noun current avatar is a retained cross-stage object pointer.
evidence_for: cGameNounManager+0x54 is intrusive_ptr<cCreatureAnimal>; cCellGame+0x411c is cObjectPoolIndex into a 4096-slot cCellObjectData pool.
Cell movement/despawn resolves the index through pool lookup, while creature progression functions call 0x00b1fdb0 for a cCreature pointer.
0x00d39360 stores/compares the noun creature address, not a Cell pool index.
evidence_against: Both domains use the word avatar and both are player-facing current selections, which invites accidental conflation.
The historical current-source approximation uses a scene player and has no original noun-pointer counterpart.
adversarial_steps.independence: The two layouts and two resolution mechanisms are direct, separate observations, but they were synthesized in the same session and share the same SDK/type vocabulary; they are not independent source lineages.
adversarial_steps.repetition: The name similarity is repeated evidence of a semantic parallel, not object identity.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: Native evidence establishes that the noun-layout path carries a raw cCreatureAnimal reference while Cell carries a pool index. Introducing a stable gameplay EntityId is a modern replacement recommendation, not a recovered native contract.

adversarial_steps.name: presentation-and-save-boundary
adversarial_steps.prediction: The raw owner pointer, render handles, and Cell pool slot should not be serialized as save state. Save candidates should use noun/definition/content identities and serializable records, then reconstruct runtime pointers and presentation.
evidence_for: cGameNounManager's primary interface is a message listener/strategy/runtime manager, while cCreatureBase exposes Write/Read slots and cGameData-derived records are serializable candidates.
cCreatureBase+0xb54, model handles, cCellGFX, and cCellGame pool state are runtime presentation/runtime structures.
cCellGame+0x5190 separately holds cCellSerializableData; cCreatureGameData is a separate progression object with no direct serializer or cross-stage handoff established.
evidence_against: No positive original save/load trace or field-level round trip is available.
The exact noun record that recreates a current creature and the ordering relative to mode restoration remain unresolved.
adversarial_steps.independence: Vtable/layout eligibility, Cell serialization separation, and persistence synthesis are separate artifacts, but several reuse the same Ghidra/SDK exports and are not independent votes. Current-source comparison is not original-binary evidence.
adversarial_steps.repetition: Several reports state the content/runtime/save split; those repetitions share static limitations and are not independent runtime proof.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: Native evidence establishes separate runtime owners, cCreatureBase/cGameData serializable eligibility, and separate Cell serialization state, but it does not establish the emitted save field set. The recommendation not to persist owner+0x54, presentation handles, or Cell pool indices is modern architecture guidance until a save writer/load trace proves the native treatment.

adversarial_steps.name: architecture-dependence-and-smallest-separator
adversarial_steps.prediction: A conclusion depending only on x86 pointer width or offset coincidence should change when the receiver class changes. A conclusion supported by explicit dereference, virtual refcount, store, and release instructions should remain architecture-deciding.
evidence_for: The 32-bit architecture fixes pointer and vtable-slot width at four bytes.
The exceptional receiver changes the semantic type at the same +0x54 offset, proving that the raw body is not a universal semantic accessor.
0x00b1fd50's AddRef/store/Release order and the consumer dereferences are instruction-level facts independent of the SDK name.
evidence_against: The exact source-level reason for identical bodies at 0x00b1fdb0 and 0x01002bd0 may be intentional sharing or linker ICF and is not proven.
The formal hidden-register ABI of 0x00bff2d0 and a few decompiler signatures is imperfect.
adversarial_steps.independence: The static separator used direct Ghidra assembly, global publication/destruction, structure layouts, and consumer type evidence. These are correlated same-session observations, not independent sources; the direct instruction sequence is stronger than the typed root-publication inference.
adversarial_steps.repetition: The same offset appears in two unrelated types; that repetition is the reason not to infer semantics from offset alone.
adversarial_steps.separator_result: The local +0x54 architecture boundary is resolved conditionally by receiver layout. Root publication/liveness/equality for DAT_0167eae0 versus DAT_0167eb60 remains unresolved under follow-up-03. Runtime was not performed because it would not change the local accessor/refcount mechanics, but it remains necessary for root equality, phase, teardown, and save restoration.

resolution.native_contract_decision: At the instruction/layout level, 0x00b1fdb0 is a raw +0x54 reader.
